extracted.intended_audience: journalists, journalism students, and members of the public interested in investigative journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, practices, and programmatic priorities associated with investigative journalism as described by the organization Investigative Reporters and Editors (IRE). Covers definitional quality criteria, training topics, data-skills expectations, ethics and independence principles, and inclusivity/access goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative journalism as systematic, in‑depth, original research and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: IRE defined investigative journalism as "systematic, in-depth, and original research and reporting"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a core definitional quality criterion for work to be considered investigative journalism; emphasis on methodical, deep, and original work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unearthing of secrets
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigative journalism often involves "the unearthing of secrets"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a characteristic element of investigative work — implies digging beyond surface-level reporting to expose concealed information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavy use of public records
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigative journalism often involves "heavy use of public records"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of public records is highlighted as a typical evidence source and technique for investigative reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer-assisted reporting / data journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigative journalism as characterized by "computer assisted reporting" and NICAR's aim to foster excellence in data journalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes computational/data techniques as central tools — NICAR provides training, listservs, and conferences focused on data skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on social justice and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigative journalism commonly has "a focus on social justice and accountability"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the normative aims of investigative work: holding power to account and addressing social justice concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of government open records laws (FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: NICAR is a venue for journalists to discuss the use of government open records laws; NICAR conference includes FOIA
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical standard: effective investigative/data reporting involves knowledge of and use of open-records/FOIA processes to obtain information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical data skills (programming, census/data sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: NICAR Conference includes technical data skills such as "the use of programming languages, Census Bureau data and FOIA"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations for data journalists include ability to use programming tools, large public datasets (e.g., Census), and data-processing techniques taught at NICAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing an investigation (training topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference workshop topics included "how to manage an investigation"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training and best-practice guidance for investigative projects should cover project management, planning, timelines, and organization of complex reporting efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working as a team (training topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop topics included "how to work as a team"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team processes and collaboration are treated as an explicit skill/criterion for successful investigative projects (planning roles, coordination, communication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting specific topics (subject-matter reporting skills)
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops covered "how to report specific topics such as crime"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative reporters are expected to have or develop topic-specific reporting skills (e.g., crime reporting techniques) relevant to the subject of investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling legal and ethical issues (training topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops included "how to deal with legal and ethical issues in investigative reporting"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal/ethical competence (defamation risk, source protection, privacy, conflicts) is a core criterion taught and expected of investigative journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical oversight and continual ethical inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: IRE members voted to establish an ethics committee "responsible for raising in a continuing way the ethical questions which confront journalists" and "responsible for examining the assumptions that underlie" investigative journalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational practice/standard: continuous ethical review and a formal body to surface and examine ethical dilemmas is a quality/standards expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational openness/inclusivity in membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders debated membership restrictions and ultimately decided for openness so "even inexperienced journalists could get help from IRE"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stated organizational principle: openness and inclusivity for practitioners as part of fostering excellence and spreading best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic independence from intelligence and law‑enforcement agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Members voted to seek ending associations with the CIA, FBI, or other law enforcement agencies to maintain "American journalistic independence"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative standard: maintain independence from government/intelligence/law-enforcement institutions to protect editorial independence and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative cross‑newsroom investigations as a model
rubrics_metrics.description: The Arizona Project: a 38‑journalist team from 28 outlets produced a 23‑part series exposing state corruption
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates a practice/standard where large-scale collaborative investigations across organizations are effective and sometimes necessary for major accountability reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessible training for underserved communities
rubrics_metrics.description: AccessFest focuses on "diversity, belonging, equity and inclusion" and aims at providing "accessible training in investigative and data reporting to underserved communities"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic standard: training and capacity-building efforts should prioritize DEI and accessibility so that underserved journalists can access investigative/data-reporting skills.
